images.filename: Season's Greetings from Midwest National Parks 2022 (806972e8-3d5b-405b-ad03-2913ce4dfb9b).jpg
images.caption:
Photo collage featuring images from seven national parks in the Midwest from left to right top to bottom. Image one: the head of a bison pokes out from behind a wayfinding sign. The bison is standing in the snow. Image two: a brick path leading through a snow-covered lawn leads to the door of a two story yellow building. Image three: A pumpkin, onions, two lanterns, wreath-like arrangement, candle, and cutting board rest on a wooden table beside a fireplace. Image four: A dome-shaped earthen lodge with a wood-framed door covered in snow. Image five: light shimmers from a river flowing through a snow-covered forest. Image six: Two wood-sided buildings sit on grounds inside a fence made of sharp wooden poles. The buildings and fence are beside a large lake. Image seven: A long multi-story brown building made of brick with terraces creating a high point at the center. Ramped walkways lead to an entrances below arches at the center. Text at the bottom reads, "Season's Greetings. Midwest National Parks."
Season's greetings and happy solstice from your Midwest national parks! We hope these photos bring brightness and cheer to the shortest day of the year!
From left to right, top to bottom: Image one: A bison stands next to a sign at Wind Cave National Park. NPS. Image two: The season's first snowfall at William Howard Taft National Historic Site. NPS / Ruth Horstman. Image three: Holiday decorations and a fire create a festive mood during an evening program at Lincoln Boyhood National Memorial. NPS / Bob Marshall. Image four: Earth lodge covered in snow at Knife River Indian Villages National Historic Site. NPS. Image five: Snow-covered river banks at Mississippi National River and Recreation Area. NPS / Gordon Dietzman. Image six: The Great Hall and company kitchen at Grand Portage National Monument. NPS / Gilaine Spoto. Image seven: Snow falls at Little Rock Central High School National Historic Site. NPS.
